<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Sp1nd01" />{{rh|A cup put in|Geneſis.|Beniamins ſacke.}} {{rule}} <!-- useful info for KJV Common characters: ſ ¶ ⁊ ⸗ <sup>†</sup>{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=† ''Note text''}} *{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=* Note text}} ‖{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=‖ ''Note text''}}  Remember that v and u are combined, "v" appears at beginnings of words and "u" in the middle Remember that i and j are combined, use "i" or "I" in all cases.--></noinclude>{{verse|43|28}}And they anſwered, Thy ſeruant our father {{smaller|is}} in good health, hee {{smaller|is}} yet aliue: ⁊ they bowed downe their heads, and made a obeiſance.

{{verse|43|29}}And he lift vp his eyes, and ſawe his brother Beniamin, his mothers ſonne, and ſaid, {{smaller|Is}} this your yonger brother, of whom yee ſpake vnto mee? and he ſaid, God be gracious vnto thee, my ſonne.

{{verse|43|30}}And Ioſeph made haſte: for his bowels did yerne vpon his brother: and he ſought {{smaller|where}} to weepe, and hee entred into {{smaller|his}} chamber, ⁊ wept there.

{{verse|43|31}}And he waſhed his face, and went out, and refrained himſelfe, and ſaide, Set on bread.

{{verse|43|32}}And they ſet on for him by himſelfe, and for them by themſelues, and for the Egyptians which did eate with him, by themſelues: becauſe the Egyptians might not eate bread with the Hebrewes: for that {{smaller|is}} an abomination vnto the Egyptians.

{{verse|43|33}}And they ſate before him, the firſt borne according to his birthright, and the yongeſt according to his youth: and the men maruelled one at another.

{{verse|43|34}}And hee tooke and {{smaller|ſent}} meaſſes vnto them from before him: but Beniamins meaſſe {{smaller|was}} fiue times ſo much as any of theirs: and they drunke, and <sup>†</sup>{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=† ''Heb. they dranke largely.''}} were merry with him.

==={{Chapter|44|CHAP. XLIIII.}}===

{{smaller block|[[#44:1|1]] Ioſephs policie to ſtay his brethren. [[#44:14|14]] Iudahs humble ſupplication to Ioſeph.}}

{{verse|44|1|notext=}}
{{dropinitial|A|image=King James Bible (1611) page A1v (A).png|imgsize=100px}}Nd hee commaunded the <sup>†</sup>{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=† ''Heb. him that was ouer his houſe''}} ſteward of his houſe, ſaying, Fill the mens ſackes {{smaller|with}} food, as much as they can carie, and put euery mans money in his ſacks mouth.

{{verse|44|2}}And put my cup, the ſiluer cup, in the ſackes mouth of the yongeſt, and his corne money: and he did according to the word that Ioſeph had ſpoken.

{{verse|44|3}}Aſſoone as the morning was light, the men were ſent away, they, and their aſſes.

{{verse|44|4}}And when they were gone out of the citie, and not {{smaller|yet}} farre off, Ioſeph ſaid vnto his ſteward, Vp, follow after the men; and when thou doeſt ouertake them, ſay vnto them, Wherefore haue ye rewarded euill for good?

{{verse|44|5}}{{smaller|Is}} not this {{smaller|it}}, in which my lord drinketh? and whereby indeed he ‖{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=‖ ''Or, maketh triall.''}} diuineth? ye haue done euill in ſo doing.

{{verse|44|6}}¶ And he ouertooke them, and he ſpake vnto them theſe ſame words.

{{verse|44|7}}And they ſaid vnto him, wherefore ſaith my lord theſe words? God forbid that thy ſeruants ſhould doe according to this thing.

{{verse|44|8}}Behold, the money which wee found in our ſackes mouthes, wee brought againe vnto thee, out of the land of Canaan: how then ſhould wee ſteale out of thy lords houſe, ſiluer or golde?

{{verse|44|9}}With whom {{smaller|ſoeuer}} of thy ſeruants it be found, both let him die, and we alſo will be my lords bondmen.

{{verse|44|10}}And he ſaid, Now alſo {{smaller|let}} it {{smaller|be}} according vnto your wordes: hee with whom it is found, ſhall be my ſeruant: and ye ſhall be blameleſſe.

{{verse|44|11}}Then they ſpeedily tooke downe euery man his ſacke to the ground, and opened euery man his ſacke.

{{verse|44|12}}And he ſearched, {{smaller|and}} began at the eldeſt, and left at the yongest: and the cup was found in Beniamins ſacke.

{{verse|44|13}}Then they rent their clothes, and laded euery man his aſſe, and returned to the citie.

{{verse|44|14}}¶ And Iudah and his brethren came to Ioſephs houſe: (for he {{smaller|was}} yet there) and they fell before him on the ground.

{{verse|44|15}}And Ioſeph ſaid vnto them, What deed {{smaller|is}} this that ye haue done? Wote ye not, that ſuch a man as I can certainely <sup>†</sup>{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=† ''Or, make triall?''}} diuine?

{{verse|44|16}}And Iudah ſaid, what ſhall wee ſay vnto my lord? what ſhal we ſpeake? or how ſhall we cleare our ſelues? God hath found out the iniquitie of they ſeruants: beholde, wee are my lords ſeruants, both we, and he alſo with whom the cup is found.

{{verse|44|17}}And he ſaid, God forbid that I ſhould doe ſo: {{smaller|but}} the man in whoſe hand the cup is found, he ſhal be my ſeruant; and as for you, get you vp in peace vnto your father.

{{verse|44|18}}¶ Then Iudah came neere vnto him, and ſaid, Oh my lord, let thy ſeruant, I pray thee, ſpeake a word in my lords eares, ⁊ let not thine anger burne againſt thy ſeruant: for thou {{smaller|art}} euen as Pharaoh.

{{verse|44|19}}My lord aſked his ſeruants, ſaying, Haue ye a father, or a brother?

{{verse|44|20}}And we ſaid vnto my lord, Wee haue a father, an olde man, and a childe<noinclude>{{right|of}}</noinclude>
